# REAL vLLM /metrics scrape. Captured, not written by hand.
#
# Provenance:
#   image        vllm/vllm-openai-cpu@sha256:0314b8a7594a3fc54e8a0c3ca1ba0c9257302bfb546abfb49a2d6107d2d0767f
#                (tag vllm/vllm-openai-cpu:v0.27.1-x86_64)
#   vllm         0.27.1     torch 2.13.0+cpu     python 3.12.13
#   model        Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct  --dtype bfloat16 --max-model-len 1024 --max-num-seqs 16
#   captured     2026-08-23, x86_64 CPU host, under 48 concurrent streaming requests
#
# This replaces the synthetic fixture that stood here while no vLLM had ever been run. That fixture
# was written from the documentation, so it could only ever confirm what the documentation says --
# which is the failure class this repository keeps finding. Three of its assumptions were wrong:
#
#   vllm:gpu_cache_usage_perc   absent in 0.27.1. The V0 alias the parser falls back to no longer
#                               exists upstream; that fallback is now dead weight kept only for
#                               older servers, and this file cannot exercise it.
#   vllm:num_requests_swapped   absent. The V1 engine does not swap, so the series was removed.
#   integer-formatted gauges    the fixture wrote "5"; a real server writes "32.0". Both parse, but
#                               only one is what arrives on the wire.
#
# It also surfaced a hazard no documentation reading would have produced: 0.27.1 added
# vllm:num_requests_waiting_by_reason, whose name has vllm:num_requests_waiting as a strict prefix.
# Any reader matching by prefix rather than by exact family name now silently reads two families.
#
# The CPU build is not the GPU build. Values here are a CPU server's (kv usage is near zero because
# VLLM_CPU_KVCACHE_SPACE is large relative to a 0.5B model), so this file pins names, types, label
# sets and formatting -- not magnitudes. Recapture on the paid GPU run to pin magnitudes too.
